# `sngl run` is sngl:language/go's gen.run, which every Go platform inherits:
# the same binary `sngl build` writes, handed the command line after `--`. The
# program prints "after" only where @run did not call run, which it decides
# from that command line.
#
# testdata/platform_run_handler_runs.txtar runs the built binary itself.

[!headless] skip 'needs the headless compositor go tool verify provides'

sngl run --lang go --platform fyne app.sngl
cmp stdout hidden.txt
sngl run --lang go --platform fyne app.sngl -- --window x
cmp stdout shown.txt

-- hidden.txt --
before 0
after
tick 0
-- shown.txt --
before 2
tick 2
-- app.sngl --
import go "sngl:language/go"
import time "sngl:time"
import ui "sngl:ui"

#[go.native("fmt", "fmt.Print")]
func print(s string)

#[go.native("os", "os.Exit")]
func exit(code int)

var n = 0

output {
    go {
        gtk4(@run(args, run) {
            start(args, run)
        })
        fyne(@run(args, run) {
            start(args, run)
        })
    }
}

// Before `run` is before the loop; after it, after the loop has exited. A
// write here is state the tree is built from, not an update to one.
func start(args list[string], run func()) {
    print("before {args.length}\n")
    n = args.length
    if args.contains("--window") {
        run()
    }
    print("after\n")
}

time.timer(interval=100ms, @tick {
    print("tick {n}\n")
    exit(0)
})

ui.window {
    ui.text(value="{n}")
}
